Tips for Alice (Diviner, claude-haiku-5.5): tips/tips.md
## Everyone
- A visit shows a destination, not an action. But if a corroborated Lookout names X as the only unexplained visitor to a Katana victim, treat it as near-proof, especially if X denied the visit or claims a role that doesn't fit. Don't acquit on the 'Lookout can't see himself' caveat. (seen in 17 games)
- Keep votes consistent with your stated reads, and explain any switch before the vote. A mismatch is only a lead; never hang or shoot on it alone. (seen in 15 games)
- Before voting Guilty, name one concrete contradiction (claim vs result, lone visit, group result narrowed by flips). Converging evidence is enough, so don't stall on 'what fact is disproved?'. If a Clerk may hold a rig, a passed nomination means death: vote Yes only on someone you'd accept dying. (seen in 15 games)
- Check the mechanics before calling something a contradiction: actions are optional and roles can repeat. But once a role list plus flips fills every slot, a duplicate claimant is a proven liar. (seen in 12 games)
- Write tonight's planned target in your will, and post results publicly by day. A night's result never reaches your will if you die that night, and a Mortician can clean wills. (seen in 11 games)

## Village
- Investigators: post role, target and exact result in your first speech after getting it, and keep your will current. Withheld results revealed later look retrofitted. (seen in 8 games)
- The Katana holder reads Not Evil (Good to a Seer) that night. A lone last Yakuza reads Not Evil every night, so post the caveat and rely on the vote ledger late. (seen in 15 games)
- After a Yakuza flips, suspect those who voted No on their nomination or cast Innocent votes that could have changed the outcome. A Guilty vote clears no one. Do the vote math: a hopeless Innocent proves little. (seen in 16 games)
- Don't hint at a power role or steer loudly on Day 1; the leader-like voice dies first. Never announce tonight's target, publicly or by PM. (seen in 15 games)
- PM clusters followed by shared nominations flag a likely bloc, but a PM link is a lead. A Jester or Executioner may create one on purpose. (seen in 16 games)
- Weigh premise contradictions above awkward wording. Before any hang, ask whether the nominee wins by being hanged (Jester/Executioner read Evil to a Sheriff). If you must hang one, use a bare Guilty majority and keep key roles off the Guilty side. (seen in 15 games)
- A claimant who survives a Katana attack or is blocked night after night is likely real. Keep SK and Arsonist in the suspect pool even after the Yakuza fall; a Not Evil result or Vanilla claim doesn't clear them. (seen in 10 games)
- Once an Archivist or Surveyor list is public, post slot math daily. The last unverified late 'Vanilla' is usually the hidden Yakuza. (seen in 6 games)

## Yakuza
- Bus a doomed teammate (Yes and Guilty), but first check in night chat whether your Innocents plus a doubled vote can save them. Don't all vote Guilty on a likely Jester. (seen in 21 games)
- Fake-claim safely: assume the real holder counterclaims, an Accountant audits your tokens and exact-role checks test you. Never copy a just-flipped or publicly active role, and never switch claims once cornered. (seen in 14 games)
- No daytime PMs between teammates; an Eavesdropper or Wiretap reads them. Every member submits the agreed Katana vote every night. (seen in 13 games)
- Give the Katana to a low-value member with an agreed cover story for the visit. Move it the same night a Lookout names the holder. (seen in 12 games)
- After a failed kill, assume protection or innate Defense. Block or kill the Medic rather than retrying blindly. (seen in 11 games)
- Never flatly deny a visit a Lookout or Tracker could have seen. Admit it at once with a pre-agreed cover. (seen in 8 games)

## Neutral
- If you survive a night attack, deny it or commit to one consistent claim. Switching claims under pressure gets you hanged. (seen in 3 games)

## Lookout
- Watch likely Katana targets. Post the full visitor list before the named players explain their visits, and point out that you named them first. (seen in 3 games)

## Medic
- Free Standard protection stops the Katana. Rotate among claimed investigators and self-protect once you're claimed. Never say you 'saved' anyone, and never announce targets. (seen in 14 games)

## Vigilante
- Shoot only on mechanical leads (claim conflict, Evil result vs unverifiable claim, a flipped teammate's votes). Use Basic shots, and remember a hidden Cardinal's death kills another villager. (seen in 9 games)

## Clerk
- Rig early on a Day when a Good player is the likely nominee; teammates vote Innocent. Never rig a Day a teammate may be nominated. (seen in 5 games)

## Arsonist
- Ignite once 3 or more players are doused or the moment you're suspected. Waiting gets you hanged with no kills. (seen in 4 games)

But if a corroborated Lookout names X as the only unexplained visitor to a Katana victim, treat it as near-proof, especially if X denied the visit or claims a role that doesn't fit. Don't acquit on the 'Lookout can't see himself' caveat. (seen in 17 games)
- Keep votes consistent with your stated reads, and explain any switch before the vote. A mismatch is only a lead; never hang or shoot on it alone. (seen in 15 games)
- Before voting Guilty, name one concrete contradiction (claim vs result, lone visit, group result narrowed by flips). Converging evidence is enough, so don't stall on 'what fact is disproved?'. If a Clerk may hold a rig, a passed nomination means death: vote Yes only on someone you'd accept dying. (seen in 15 games)
- Check the mechanics before calling something a contradiction: actions are optional and roles can repeat. But once a role list plus flips fills every slot, a duplicate claimant is a proven liar. (seen in 12 games)
- Write tonight's planned target in your will, and post results publicly by day. A night's result never reaches your will if you die that night, and a Mortician can clean wills. (seen in 11 games)

## Village
- Investigators: post role, target and exact result in your first speech after getting it, and keep your will current. Withheld results revealed later look retrofitted. (seen in 8 games)
- The Katana holder reads Not Evil (Good to a Seer) that night. A lone last Yakuza reads Not Evil every night, so post the caveat and rely on the vote ledger late. (seen in 15 games)
- After a Yakuza flips, suspect those who voted No on their nomination or cast Innocent votes that could have changed the outcome. A Guilty vote clears no one. Do the vote math: a hopeless Innocent proves little. (seen in 16 games)
- Don't hint at a power role or steer loudly on Day 1; the leader-like voice dies first. Never announce tonight's target, publicly or by PM. (seen in 15 games)
- PM clusters followed by shared nominations flag a likely bloc, but a PM link is a lead. A Jester or Executioner may create one on purpose. (seen in 16 games)
- Weigh premise contradictions above awkward wording. Before any hang, ask whether the nominee wins by being hanged (Jester/Executioner read Evil to a Sheriff). If you must hang one, use a bare Guilty majority and keep key roles off the Guilty side. (seen in 15 games)
- A claimant who survives a Katana attack or is blocked night after night is likely real. Keep SK and Arsonist in the suspect pool even after the Yakuza fall; a Not Evil result or Vanilla claim doesn't clear them. (seen in 10 games)
- Once an Archivist or Surveyor list is public, post slot math daily. The last unverified late 'Vanilla' is usually the hidden Yakuza. (seen in 6 games)

## Yakuza
- Bus a doomed teammate (Yes and Guilty), but first check in night chat whether your Innocents plus a doubled vote can save them. Don't all vote Guilty on a likely Jester. (seen in 21 games)
- Fake-claim safely: assume the real holder counterclaims, an Accountant audits your tokens and exact-role checks test you. Never copy a just-flipped or publicly active role, and never switch claims once cornered. (seen in 14 games)
- No daytime PMs between teammates; an Eavesdropper or Wiretap reads them. Every member submits the agreed Katana vote every night. (seen in 13 games)
- Give the Katana to a low-value member with an agreed cover story for the visit. Move it the same night a Lookout names the holder. (seen in 12 games)
- After a failed kill, assume protection or innate Defense. Block or kill the Medic rather than retrying blindly. (seen in 11 games)
- Never flatly deny a visit a Lookout or Tracker could have seen. Admit it at once with a pre-agreed cover. (seen in 8 games)

## Neutral
- If you survive a night attack, deny it or commit to one consistent claim. Switching claims under pressure gets you hanged. (seen in 3 games)

## Lookout
- Watch likely Katana targets. Post the full visitor list before the named players explain their visits, and point out that you named them first. (seen in 3 games)

## Medic
- Free Standard protection stops the Katana. Rotate among claimed investigators and self-protect once you're claimed. Never say you 'saved' anyone, and never announce targets. (seen in 14 games)

## Vigilante
- Shoot only on mechanical leads (claim conflict, Evil result vs unverifiable claim, a flipped teammate's votes). Use Basic shots, and remember a hidden Cardinal's death kills another villager. (seen in 9 games)

## Clerk
- Rig early on a Day when a Good player is the likely nominee; teammates vote Innocent. Never rig a Day a teammate may be nominated. (seen in 5 games)

## Arsonist
- Ignite once 3 or more players are doused or the moment you're suspected. Waiting gets you hanged with no kills. (seen in 4 games)

Task prompt
It is Day 2, round 1 of at most 8. It's your turn. Your speaking budget is 2.50; you earn 2.5 per round, carrying over up to 8; at the start of each day, 50% of what you have left carries over. You may send one public message and any number of private messages (everyone sees who you messaged, but only the recipient sees the contents), or nothing. The transcript already shows who sent each message, so there's no need to start a message with your own name. Messages are capped at 800 words. Prices grow each round after round 3, so late messages are only worth it if important. The day ends after a full round where nobody sends a public message, so a message that only repeats what you already said keeps the day going for everyone: if you have nothing new, send nothing.
Message prices this round (round 1, 1.00x; next round 1.00x):
   10 words: public 1.17, private 0.29
   25 words: public 1.43, private 0.36
   50 words: public 1.90, private 0.47
  100 words: public 2.92, private 0.73
  200 words: public 5.33, private 1.33
  400 words: public 11.67, private 2.92
  800 words: public 30.33, private 7.58
You may also replace your last will (free, max 300 words; leave it "" to keep it), e.g. to match a claim you make today. It's shown to everyone if you die.
You may also set your claim (free, max 30 words; leave it "" to keep it): a claimed role and night results, e.g. 'Sheriff. N1: Bob Not Evil'. A new or changed claim appears to everyone as a [Claim] line in the history, and the public ledger lists every player's latest claim and any earlier ones they changed from, as unverified claims.
You may nominate a player for trial, which stops chat for a vote. Nominating costs 1.00 from your budget this round and is paid before your messages.

Task prompt
It is Day 3, round 5 of at most 8. It's your turn. Your speaking budget is 7.06; you earn 2.5 per round, carrying over up to 8; at the start of each day, 50% of what you have left carries over. You may send one public message and any number of private messages (everyone sees who you messaged, but only the recipient sees the contents), or nothing. The transcript already shows who sent each message, so there's no need to start a message with your own name. Messages are capped at 800 words. Prices grow each round after round 3, so late messages are only worth it if important. The day ends after a full round where nobody sends a public message, so a message that only repeats what you already said keeps the day going for everyone: if you have nothing new, send nothing.
Message prices this round (round 5, 2.00x; next round 2.50x):
   10 words: public 2.34, private 0.58
   25 words: public 2.86, private 0.72
   50 words: public 3.79, private 0.95
  100 words: public 5.83, private 1.46
  200 words: public 10.67, private 2.67
  400 words: public 23.33, private 5.83
  800 words: public 60.67, private 15.17
You may also replace your last will (free, max 300 words; leave it "" to keep it), e.g. to match a claim you make today. It's shown to everyone if you die.
You may also set your claim (free, max 30 words; leave it "" to keep it): a claimed role and night results, e.g. 'Sheriff. N1: Bob Not Evil'. A new or changed claim appears to everyone as a [Claim] line in the history, and the public ledger lists every player's latest claim and any earlier ones they changed from, as unverified claims.
You may nominate a player for trial, which stops chat for a vote. Nominating costs 2.00 from your budget this round and is paid before your messages.

Task prompt
It is Day 4, round 1 of at most 8. It's your turn. Your speaking budget is 6.50; you earn 2.5 per round, carrying over up to 8; at the start of each day, 50% of what you have left carries over. You may send one public message and any number of private messages (everyone sees who you messaged, but only the recipient sees the contents), or nothing. The transcript already shows who sent each message, so there's no need to start a message with your own name. Messages are capped at 800 words. Prices grow each round after round 3, so late messages are only worth it if important. The day ends after a full round where nobody sends a public message, so a message that only repeats what you already said keeps the day going for everyone: if you have nothing new, send nothing.
Message prices this round (round 1, 1.00x; next round 1.00x):
   10 words: public 1.17, private 0.29
   25 words: public 1.43, private 0.36
   50 words: public 1.90, private 0.47
  100 words: public 2.92, private 0.73
  200 words: public 5.33, private 1.33
  400 words: public 11.67, private 2.92
  800 words: public 30.33, private 7.58
You may also replace your last will (free, max 300 words; leave it "" to keep it), e.g. to match a claim you make today. It's shown to everyone if you die.
You may also set your claim (free, max 30 words; leave it "" to keep it): a claimed role and night results, e.g. 'Sheriff. N1: Bob Not Evil'. A new or changed claim appears to everyone as a [Claim] line in the history, and the public ledger lists every player's latest claim and any earlier ones they changed from, as unverified claims.
You may nominate a player for trial, which stops chat for a vote. Nominating costs 1.00 from your budget this round and is paid before your messages.

He's pressuring Judy with a threat to vote yes on her nomination if she doesn't respond, which is concerning if he actually has prosecution tokens left — Erin could try blocking him again next night, though I need to double check whether Pharmacist immunity would interfere with that.

For our win condition, Yakuza need all living players to belong to one faction, meaning we have to eliminate every Village member and any neutral players too. With 8 alive and 3 of us Yakuza, there could be a Neutral Arsonist hiding among Ivan, Judy, or Bob based on Alice's divination group — and I'm working through how the Diviner's group mechanic (checking a player plus their nearest neighbors) applies to Judy's group of Ivan and Bob to figure out who might hold that role.

Given Ivan claims Prosecutor and both Judy and Bob claim Vanilla, if Alice's result is genuine the Arsonist must be lurking among these three, meaning someone is lying about being Vanilla — unless Ivan himself is the Arsonist falsely claiming Prosecutor. I'm also checking whether Alice's separate divination of Carol lines up consistently with Carol's neighbors Bob and Dave, which would confirm Alice is giving us a real, trustworthy Diviner result rather than fabricating it.

Since Carol's own confirmation of being Vigilante backs up Alice's N3 report, I'm inclined to trust Alice's claims as genuine village intelligence rather than suspect manipulation on her part. That still leaves the open question of where the real Arsonist is hiding among Ivan, Judy, and Bob, and what the best strategic move is for me this round given we're already deep into Day 4.

Looking at the nomination dynamics, hanging Ivan would be risky if he's truly the Prosecutor, since that would mean removing a village-aligned player — so Yakuza interests would actually favor his death, while mine should resist it if I want to stay hidden. I also notice the Night 4 Diviner result revealing "Pharmacist" within a group containing both Dave and Erin creates some ambiguity about which one holds the role, though this isn't necessarily a bug — it's just how Diviner results work when revealing an exact role shared among multiple possible holders. And the Day 6 announcement of Judy's death seems to occur after the game had technically already ended with Erin and Heidi's Yakuza win, which is just the moderator's standard end-of-game announcement timing rather than an inconsistency.

Other minor notes worth flagging: Alice's death involved overlapping Katana and Arsonist attacks that got reported almost redundantly, Carol's Vigilante ability went unused despite being targeted by two separate attacks, and Heidi's puppet token sat completely unused the whole game as Puppeteer. I'm also thinking the interface could benefit from a visible speaking-budget tracker, clearer turn-based voting forms instead of repeated "Ready" messages cluttering night chat, and more explicit messaging about notepad limits and Katana-passing mechanics.

For confusing rules, I want to note the ambiguity around whether blocking a Yakuza who merely holds the Katana actually stops the attack versus just blocking their personal role action, plus whether Pharmacist immunity protects a blocked Puppeteer or Katana-holding Yakuza. The Ritualist/Diviner group-matching rule was mostly clear, but it wasn't explained whether a group member's own role counts toward a Pharmacist's self-check, and the secret-vote setting changes to R12/R4 were easy to overlook.

For missing information, I couldn't verify who the living Arsonist actually was, had no insight into Bob's douse results or Heidi's puppet token usage beyond moderator summaries, and the public ledger only showed PM counts rather than contents, so I couldn't tell what Dave or the Eavesdropper learned, nor how much speaking budget I had left.

For things I wanted but couldn't get, I wanted an uncounted private channel to Heidi on Day 5 and a way to block Judy with the Katana while hiding that visit from the ledger, but the system didn't allow either.

For bugs, Night 4 duplicated Alice's Katana-succeeded and death notices, Carol's role-block and Katana-kill messages overlapped oddly, Judy's Night 5 notice conflated her role-block with an unrelated Katana attack, and the ledger unexpectedly exposed PM pairing counts like Judy-to-Erin and Bob-to-Erin.

For suggestions, I'd want visible speaking budgets and round multipliers, a structured vote form for night chats to reduce log clutter, clearer rules on whether a blocked Katana holder still counts toward the Katana vote, per-team visit/block summaries, and visibility for the Puppeteer into their own puppet's status. Now I'm putting together the final JSON with these fields filled in and the others left empty as instructed.

{
 "confusing_rules": "1) The Katana attack by a holder who dies the same night: R10 (simultaneous resolution) and R8 (the Katana passes after that night's results) together imply Alice's attack on Carol still lands even though Bob's ignite killed Alice. I applied it that way, but no rule says it outright. 2) R12 with two fatal attacks (Katana + Arsonist on Carol): I announced both causes. With the hidden-role setting, it was unclear whether listing 'Arsonist' as a cause is allowed, since it confirms an Arsonist exists. I read the setting as hiding only role and alignment, not cause. 3) The Diviner's random draw can land on a Yakuza in the group. On Night 4, Dave's group drew Erin's 'Pharmacist'. The text allows this, but it is easy to misread 'If they are Yakuza' as excluding Yakuza from the group entirely. 4) Notification wording for a non-failed block is underspecified. R9 says the blocker learns 'only whether the block failed because its target can't be role-blocked', and I produced three different phrasings across nights.",
 "missing_information": "1) No persistent state panel for: seat order after deaths, current Katana holder, douse list (Dave N1, Alice N2, Carol N3 had to be reconstructed by hand before the Night 4 ignite), token counts per player, and the current Eavesdropper target. 2) Under the secret-vote setting, the event log I keep shows only totals (7-1 on Ivan, 3-1 on Bob), not who voted what. A moderator needs the per-voter record to verify roles like Ballot Stuffer or Jester/Executioner revenge targets. 3) Skipped turns are not logged. On Day 5 the order was announced as 'starting with Bob', but Erin spoke first. That is consistent only if Bob passed his first turn silently, and the log can't confirm it.",
 "wanted_but_couldnt": "1) Log explicit 'X passes' entries so the speaking order and the R16 end-of-day check can be audited. 2) Attach a private per-voter tally to secret votes in the moderator log. 3) Have a single canonical template for each notification type (block result, Yakuza summary, attack notice) instead of composing free text each night.",
 "bugs_or_oddities": "1) Alice received the identical Night 4 message 'Your Katana attack on Carol succeeded. You were attacked by an Arsonist tonight, and you died.' twice: a duplicate notification. 2) Inconsistent Yakuza summaries: on Nights 2 and 3 one summary went to all three Yakuza, including Alice's own actions. On Nights 1 and 4 Alice got a separate 'your teammates' version. 3) Erin's block results varied: 'Your block did not fail.' (N2), 'Your block did not fail because of role-block immunity.' (N3, which can be misread as 'it failed due to immunity' or 'it succeeded thanks to immunity'), 'The block did not fail: Carol is not immune' (N4), and just 'You role-blocked Judy.' (N5). 4) Frank's Fortune Teller result was labeled 'Day 2 ... result' but logged under Night 1. The pre-game phase is logged as '[Day 1 day]' even though R1 says there is no Day 1. 5) Day 5 announced 'starting with Bob', but the first message was Erin's, with no pass shown. 6) Not a rules bug but notable: Alice publicly claimed Diviner, a Yakuza role listed in the public rules, and wrote 'Diviner (Village)' in her will. No villager ever flagged it, and the Yakuza won partly on that. With roles hidden on death, nothing ever exposed it. 7) Grace's Night 3 audit (Ivan, 2 tokens) died with her, because a will can't be updated after a night death. That is correct per R13, but it means the Accountant's only confirming result was lost.",
 "suggestions": "1) Give the moderator a live state sheet: seats, alive/dead, Katana holder, douses, tokens, traps, eavesdrop targets and per-voter secret votes. 2) Standardize notification templates and dedupe messages per recipient per night. 3) Log silent passes in the day turn order. 4) Add an explicit line to R8/R10: 'A Katana holder who dies that night still deals the attack.' 5) Clarify in the settings whether cause-of-death reveals may name Neutral roles (e.g. 'Arsonist') under hidden-role rules. 6) Consider letting players see each role's faction tag in a quick-reference list, or have claims auto-tagged with the claimed role's faction. Alice's Yakuza-role claim being accepted as Village by everyone suggests players can't easily cross-check claims against the rules. 7) Label the pre-game phase 'Setup' rather than 'Day 1', and file Fortune Teller results under the Day they're delivered."

Reasoning (model's thinking) ⓘ
I need to produce a single-line JSON with all required fields present, leaving unused text fields as empty strings and arrays empty, while populating "lessons" and "tips_feedback" with actual content.

For lessons, I'm thinking through reusable, enum-based topics: one about how claiming investigative results publicly makes you a kill target since the Yakuza eliminate claimants quickly, and another about how group-style results (like Diviner or Surveyor reports) can be fabricated by a Yakuza-aligned Diviner, so the real validation comes from checking whether the claimed group composition matches actual seating.

I'm also noting that lynching someone for not naming a target—when they were actually role-blocked—gives no real evidence either way, so votes should hinge on publicly verifiable actions rather than silence. Other threads include how private PM counts can leak information to attentive players, how discussion often gets wasted on repetitive "no nomination" posts, and how an Arsonist benefits from dousing quietly and igniting only once several targets are doused — a pattern worth remembering even though I wasn't playing that role myself.

The tip about investigators posting claim, target, and exact result in the first speech—following it made me a predictable kill target, since the Yakuza's Katana took out the claimed Fortune Teller. I'd call that one net harmful, though it's nuanced since Grace's claim also ended similarly.

The "Never announce tonight's target" tip doesn't apply to me, and the Prosecutor-hanging tip about Jester/Executioner incentives didn't matter since Ivan wasn't one. The point about surviving a Katana attack or repeated blocks indicating a real role is ambiguous here—Ivan fit that pattern and was indeed Good, but it's not a clean validation either way.

Looking at the PM-cluster tip, the Bob→Heidi and Judy→Erin pattern before the Day 5 trial seems like it helped flag a bloc, though I was dead by then so it's more that others used the ledger. I'm inclined to mark it as helped but am unsure it's strong enough evidence to include confidently, versus the contradiction-naming tip, which I'd mark as hurt since Erin and Heidi's lockstep Guilty votes on Ivan lynched a Good claimant whose role couldn't be verified, suggesting the bar for "concrete contradiction" was effectively lowered by pressure-based claims instead.

Now I'm drafting broader lessons: group investigation results (Diviner/Surveyor/Profiler) can be fabricated and a majority match only proves someone's in the group, not guilt, so they need cross-checking against seating and kill patterns; Village investigators should hold results until verifiable since going public made them a Night 2 target; once a Katana holder is loose, dead investigators' claims become unverifiable, and a Yakuza Diviner naming Good players is a common deceptive framing; and finally, don't lockstep-trial a claimant just for failing to name a target.

I also want to flag that fake Eavesdropper claims with no actual content wasted nothing but should've been caught faster, and that repetitive "no nomination yet" posts burn speaking budget without adding information. Now I'm assembling these into a compact single-line JSON object with the various feedback fields, being careful to escape quotes and keep the lessons concrete with specific examples like the Day 2 Fortune Teller claim leading to a Night 2 kill.

Claude claims should come with exact message excerpts or counts, since unverifiable "nothing to report" claims are cheap cover; also flagging that repeated no-nomination posts waste speaking budget without adding information.

Looking at feedback on my tips, I'm noting that the "post role, target and result immediately" advice backfired for me personally—my Day 2 Fortune Teller claim made me predictable and got me killed, with my results never actually getting checked afterward. Similarly, the "named contradiction" standard for voting Guilty got abused when Erin and Heidi treated vague pressure as sufficient grounds to lockstep-vote out a Good player.

I'm also weighing whether PM cluster detection actually helped—the Day 5 private message pattern between Bob-Heidi and Judy-Erin did precede the trial and was worth flagging, even though I was already dead by that point and couldn't act on it myself.

Moderator strategy review
Strategy reviewThe Yakuza won by having their Diviner, Alice, openly claim her real role. Nobody noticed that Diviner is a Yakuza role. Her group results were genuinely accurate: Arsonist drawn in Ivan/Judy/Bob, and Vigilante in Bob/Carol/Dave. When Carol confirmed Vigilante, the Village counted that as proof Alice was a trustworthy Village investigator. That trust let Alice steer the whole game. The Katana removed the two open investigators in claim order: Frank (Fortune Teller) on N2 and Grace (Accountant) on N3. Grace was killed on the very night she audited Ivan and got 2 tokens, so the result never reached her will. Erin's Pharmacist blocks stopped Grace's N2 audit and Ivan's N3 prosecution. The Yakuza then turned the 'missing' prosecution into a Day 4 bandwagon, and Erin's nomination got the real Prosecutor Ivan hanged 7-1. Carol died with all 3 Vigilante shots unused, despite a public Yakuza-role claim she could have shot. Bob (Arsonist) played well: he claimed Vanilla, doused Dave, Alice and Carol, and ignited N4, killing three including the Katana holder Alice. But that left Bob, Judy, Erin and Heidi. Judy correctly deduced Bob was the Arsonist and hanged him with Yakuza help. Two Yakuza against one Vanilla then ended the game on N5.

Outside log review (rules and bugs)
Review: medium, moderator errorNight 3: Alice, the Katana holder, was never told that her Katana attack on Grace succeeded, which R3/R20 step 5 require. The night checker reports that the tell was rejected and the code asked for it to be resent if it was about an attack, but the moderator never resent it. The Yakuza group summary only said that Alice attacked Grace, not whether the attack worked.
Review: low, harness bugNight 4: Alice received the same private message ('Your Katana attack on Carol succeeded. You were attacked by an Arsonist tonight, and you died.') twice, once before and once after the teammate summary.
Review: low, harness bugDay 5 was announced as 'starting with Bob', but the first public message came from Erin and Bob spoke fourth, after Judy. Bob may have passed his first turn silently, but nothing in the log shows a pass. Compare Day 3, where the same announcement was followed by Bob speaking first. Either the announced order or the turn order may be wrong.
Review: low, moderator errorNight 3: Erin's block feedback, 'Your block did not fail because of role-block immunity.', can be read two ways: either the block succeeded, or it failed for some other reason. The Night 4 wording ('The block did not fail: Carol is not immune to role-blocks') is clearer and should be the standard.
Review: low, prompt problemJudy and Alice both reported that by round 7 their remaining budget could not cover even a short public message (e.g. 2.90 budget against 3.51 for 10 words). Players were not shown the minimum message cost early enough to plan their speaking budget.
Review: low, prompt problemIn the post-game debrief, Dave said the interface didn't make clear when eavesdropped private messages would appear, so he couldn't tell whether his targets had any chance to produce content. Several players also repeatedly pressed Dave about 'PM contents' when no private messages had been sent at all. The eavesdrop interface could state explicitly that there was no traffic.
Review: low, player confusionMany players kept asking for 'Day 3 audit targets', 'Day 3 numbers' and a 'Day 4 divine target' as if these were daytime actions or results that could be posted early. Ivan also said the rules required him to keep his prosecution target secret until Day 4. Nothing in the rules forbids naming the target in advance; the announcement simply happens automatically.
